brief: Persian Gulf oil exports have recovered to their 2025 average, driven by rising Saudi crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, while China's crude imports stay weak. This supports Goldman's base case for Brent to fall to $85/bbl by year-end and $80/bbl in 2027. Diesel supply has been less resilient, and contemplated US export restrictions would push domestic diesel prices moderately lower near-term but could raise ex-US diesel and eventual US retail gasoline prices. Lower oil should ease US inflation: following softer August core PCE, Goldman now expects 3.0% core PCE this year (Q4/Q4), below the FOMC median's 3.4%, and pushed back its next-hike call to December from October, seeing a strong chance no further hikes are needed given a stable labor market. Main risks to the constructive view are higher yields and energy prices. Elsewhere, Japanese policy shifts and reallocation flows raised the case for long JPY, with 3/6/12m USD/JPY forecasts cut to 158/155/150. AI hyperscaler capex is seen beating the $1.2tn 2027 consensus though upside surprises slow, and prediction markets imply a likely Democratic Congress, with Brazil's election headed to a runoff.
